title: 01. Fundamentals: String Methods — Check/Validation (is___)
summary: Python strings have a set of is___() methods that check the nature/type of characters in the string. All return True or False.
objectives: Critical: All is___() return False for empty strings!

sections.title: CONCEPT EXPLANATION
sections.body:
Python strings have a set of **`is___()` methods** that check the nature/type of characters in the string. All return `True` or `False`.

### Complete `is___()` Methods Reference:

| Method | Returns True When... | Edge Case |
|---|---|---|
| `.isalpha()` | ALL chars are letters | Empty string → `False` |
| `.isdigit()` | ALL chars are digits (0-9) | `"²"` (superscript) → `True`! |
| `.isnumeric()` | ALL chars are numeric | `"½"` → `True`, wider than isdigit |
| `.isdecimal()` | ALL chars are decimal digits | Strictest: only 0-9 |
| `.isalnum()` | ALL chars are letters OR digits | No spaces/symbols |
| `.isspace()` | ALL chars are whitespace | Tabs, newlines count |
| `.isupper()` | ALL cased chars are uppercase | Non-letters ignored |
| `.islower()` | ALL cased chars are lowercase | Non-letters ignored |
| `.istitle()` | Title Case format | |
| `.isidentifier()` | Valid Python identifier | `"for"` → `True` (keyword!) |
| `.isprintable()` | ALL chars are printable | No `\n`, `\t`, etc. |
| `.isascii()` | ALL chars are ASCII (0-127) | |

### ⚠️ Critical: All `is___()` return `False` for empty strings!
```python
"".isalpha()   # False — empty string is NOT all-letters
"".isspace()   # False — empty string is NOT all-space
```

### ⚠️ `isdigit()` vs `isnumeric()` vs `isdecimal()`:
```python
"123".isdecimal()   # True  — strictest
"123".isdigit()     # True
"123".isnumeric()   # True  — most lenient

"²".isdecimal()     # False — superscript 2
"²".isdigit()       # True  — it IS a digit representation
"²".isnumeric()     # True

"½".isdecimal()     # False
"½".isdigit()       # False — fraction character
"½".isnumeric()     # True  — it IS numeric

# For user input validation (only 0-9), use isdecimal()!
```

sections.title: 5 EXAMPLES
sections.body:
### Example 1: All `is___()` Methods Demonstrated
```python
test_strings = {
    "hello":     "pure letters",
    "12345":     "pure digits",
    "hello123":  "letters+digits",
    "Hello":     "title-ish",
    "HELLO":     "all uppercase",
    "hello world": "with space",
    "   \t\n":   "whitespace only",
    "Hello123!": "mixed with symbol",
    "":          "empty string",
    "my_var":    "identifier-like",
}

methods = [
    ("isalpha",      str.isalpha),
    ("isdigit",      str.isdigit),
    ("isdecimal",    str.isdecimal),
    ("isnumeric",    str.isnumeric),
    ("isalnum",      str.isalnum),
    ("isspace",      str.isspace),
    ("isupper",      str.isupper),
    ("islower",      str.islower),
    ("istitle",      str.istitle),
    ("isidentifier", str.isidentifier),
    ("isascii",      str.isascii),
]

print(f"{'String':<18}", end="")
for name, _ in methods:
    print(f"{name[:6]:<8}", end="")
print()
print("-" * 100)

for s, desc in test_strings.items():
    display = repr(s)[:17]
    print(f"{display:<18}", end="")
    for _, method in methods:
        result = "T" if method(s) else "F"
        print(f"{result:<8}", end="")
    print(f"  ({desc})")
```

### Example 2: Input Validation Using `is___()` Methods
```python
def validate_user_registration(data):
    """
    Validate user registration form data.
    Returns dict of field → error message.
    """
    errors = {}

    # Validate name: letters and spaces only
    name = data.get("name", "").strip()
    if not name:
        errors["name"] = "Name is required"
    elif not all(c.isalpha() or c.isspace() for c in name):
        errors["name"] = "Name must contain only letters and spaces"
    elif len(name) < 2:
        errors["name"] = "Name must be at least 2 characters"

    # Validate age: must be numeric
    age_str = data.get("age", "").strip()
    if not age_str:
        errors["age"] = "Age is required"
    elif not age_str.isdecimal():   # isdecimal() — only 0-9!
        errors["age"] = "Age must be a whole number"
    elif not (1 <= int(age_str) <= 120):
        errors["age"] = "Age must be between 1 and 120"

    # Validate username: must be valid identifier
    username = data.get("username", "").strip()
    if not username:
        errors["username"] = "Username is required"
    elif not username.isidentifier():
        errors["username"] = "Username: letters, digits, underscores only, start with letter/underscore"
    elif username.lower() in {"admin", "root", "null", "system"}:
        errors["username"] = "Username not allowed"

    # Validate phone: digits only, 10 digits
    phone = data.get("phone", "").strip().replace("-", "").replace(" ", "")
    if not phone:
        errors["phone"] = "Phone is required"
    elif not phone.isdecimal():
        errors["phone"] = "Phone must contain only digits"
    elif len(phone) != 10:
        errors["phone"] = "Phone must be exactly 10 digits"

    return errors

# Test cases
test_data = [
    {"name": "Alice Smith",   "age": "28", "username": "alice_dev", "phone": "9876543210"},
    {"name": "Bob123",        "age": "35", "username": "bob",       "phone": "98765"},
    {"name": "",              "age": "abc","username": "2bad_start", "phone": "123-456-7890"},
    {"name": "Veerababu",     "age": "26", "username": "admin",     "phone": "9876543210"},
]

for i, data in enumerate(test_data, 1):
    errors = validate_user_registration(data)
    status = "✅ VALID" if not errors else f"❌ {len(errors)} error(s)"
    print(f"\nTest {i}: {status}")
    for field, msg in errors.items():
        print(f"  {field}: {msg}")
```

### Example 3: `isspace()`, `isupper()`, `islower()` in Text Analysis
```python
text = """Python is GREAT for Data Science.
It's FAST, FLEXIBLE, and FUN!
# This is a comment
    indented line
"""

lines = text.strip().split('\n')
print("Line Analysis:")
print(f"{'Line':<35} {'Upper%':>7} {'Lower%':>7} {'Space?':>7} {'Type':<15}")
print("-" * 75)

for line in lines:
    if not line:
        continue

    # Character type counts
    upper_count = sum(1 for c in line if c.isupper())
    lower_count = sum(1 for c in line if c.islower())
    alpha_count = sum(1 for c in line if c.isalpha())

    upper_pct = (upper_count / alpha_count * 100) if alpha_count else 0
    lower_pct = (lower_count / alpha_count * 100) if alpha_count else 0

    # Classify line
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped.startswith("#"):
        line_type = "Comment"
    elif line.startswith("    ") or line.startswith("\t"):
        line_type = "Indented"
    elif upper_pct > 70:
        line_type = "SHOUTING"
    else:
        line_type = "Normal"

    display = line.strip()[:33]
    print(f"{display:<35} {upper_pct:>6.0f}% {lower_pct:>6.0f}% "
          f"{'Yes' if line.isspace() else 'No':>7} {line_type:<15}")
```

### Example 4: `isidentifier()` for Code Generation and Validation
```python
import keyword

def validate_variable_name(name):
    """
    Validate if a string can be a Python variable name.
    Returns (is_valid, reason)
    """
    if not name:
        return False, "Empty string"

    if not name.isidentifier():
        return False, (
            f"Invalid identifier. Must start with letter or underscore, "
            f"contain only letters, digits, underscores. Got: '{name}'"
        )

    if keyword.iskeyword(name):
        return False, f"'{name}' is a Python keyword — cannot use as variable name"

    if keyword.issoftkeyword(name) if hasattr(keyword, 'issoftkeyword') else False:
        return False, f"'{name}' is a Python soft keyword"

    if name.startswith("__") and name.endswith("__"):
        return True, f"Warning: '{name}' is dunder (magic) naming convention"

    return True, "Valid variable name"

# Test various inputs
test_names = [
    "my_variable", "2bad", "class", "my-var",
    "snake_case", "CamelCase", "_private", "__dunder__",
    "for", "True", "π", "hello world", "var123"
]

print("Variable Name Validation:")
for name in test_names:
    valid, reason = validate_variable_name(name)
    icon = "✅" if valid else "❌"
    print(f"  {icon} '{name:<15}': {reason}")
```

### Example 5: Building a Strong Password Validator
```python
def analyze_password(password):
    """
    Comprehensive password analysis using is___() methods.
    Returns detailed breakdown and strength score.
    """
    if not password:
        return {"score": 0, "strength": "Empty", "details": {}}

    details = {
        "length":           len(password),
        "has_upper":        any(c.isupper() for c in password),
        "has_lower":        any(c.islower() for c in password),
        "has_digit":        any(c.isdigit() for c in password),
        "has_special":      any(not c.isalnum() for c in password),
        "all_alpha":        password.isalpha(),
        "all_digit":        password.isdigit(),
        "all_alnum":        password.isalnum(),
        "all_upper":        password.isupper(),
        "all_lower":        password.islower(),
        "count_upper":      sum(1 for c in password if c.isupper()),
        "count_lower":      sum(1 for c in password if c.islower()),
        "count_digit":      sum(1 for c in password if c.isdigit()),
        "count_special":    sum(1 for c in password if not c.isalnum()),
    }

    # Scoring
    score = 0
    feedback = []

    if details["length"] >= 8:
        score += 1
    else:
        feedback.append(f"Too short ({details['length']} chars, need 8+)")

    if details["length"] >= 12:
        score += 1   # Bonus for length

    if details["has_upper"]:
        score += 1
    else:
        feedback.append("Add uppercase letters")

    if details["has_lower"]:
        score += 1
    else:
        feedback.append("Add lowercase letters")

    if details["has_digit"]:
        score += 1
    else:
        feedback.append("Add digits")

    if details["has_special"]:
        score += 1
    else:
        feedback.append("Add special characters (!@#$%...)")

    # Penalize for all-same-type
    if details["all_alpha"] or details["all_digit"]:
        score -= 1
        feedback.append("Too uniform — mix character types")

    strength_map = {0:"Very Weak", 1:"Weak", 2:"Fair", 3:"Good", 4:"Strong", 5:"Very Strong", 6:"Excellent"}
    strength = strength_map.get(max(0, score), "Excellent")

    return {
        "score":    score,
        "strength": strength,
        "details":  details,
        "feedback": feedback
    }

passwords = ["password", "P@ssw0rd", "MyS3cur3P@ss!", "abc123", "correct horse battery staple"]
print("Password Strength Analysis:")
for pwd in passwords:
    result = analyze_password(pwd)
    bar    = "█" * result["score"] + "░" * (6 - result["score"])
    print(f"\n  '{pwd}'")
    print(f"  [{bar}] {result['strength']} (score: {result['score']}/6)")
    if result["feedback"]:
        for tip in result["feedback"]:
            print(f"    ⚠️  {tip}")
```
